title: Inside the Industrial Comeback & AI’s Power Crisis with Nigel Coe | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 37
summary: Nigel Coe describes an industrial sector split between AI/power demand and weak consumer-facing markets. He prefers nVent, Wesco and Vertiv, sees a 3M margin turnaround, and is cautious on Eaton revisions, distributors and housing. Eisman endorses the importance of earnings revisions, simple investment narratives, firm power and the scale of grid expansion. Later supplier results support the AI infrastructure and 3M operating theses; Fastenal gross margins weakened but operating margins improved. Conditional housing picks, stock-relative returns and multiyear backlog claims remain distinct from those operating validations.
assessment: Full transcript read. This episode is strongest in connecting industry structure and physical bottlenecks to operating earnings. Primary results support several guest operating theses, while stock-price causality and categorical valuation rules remain unverified.
speaker_map_notes: Nigel Coe supplies coverage-specific ratings, historical calls and most forecasts. Eisman endorses selected mechanisms and discloses GE Vernova ownership; hypothetical housing questions do not turn Coe picks into Eisman recommendations.
framework_points: Segment exposure explains why stocks sharing an AI label can have different earnings paths.
Track earnings revisions and backlog conversion, while separating business growth from multiple expansion.
Power availability can limit deployment even after construction finishes.
Turbine capacity follows a slow supply cycle and coordinated supplier investment.
Value traps and turnarounds require changing the thesis when execution and management change.
tools_and_charts: Supplier order books and backlog duration
Global industrial production and ISM PMI
Manufacturing construction and Dodge Momentum Index
transcript_cautions: Opening montage repeats the full discussion.
Guest explicitly does not cover machinery despite broad host introduction.
Many historical calls are retrospective self-reports.
Eisman ownership of GE Vernova is not a documented realized return.
Energy and power units are verbally mixed around the annual capacity illustration.
Full-year 2026 and beyond-2030 outcomes are not treated as completed.
